_guide.editing_terrain_features: Edit heightfield.features array. Three types: 'hill' (radius, height, noise — a dome), 'plateau' (radius, height, noise, flat_ratio — a dome with a flat top), 'flatten' (size or radius, falloff — levels the ground). All pos values are [X, Z] (not Y). See existing hills/plateaus/flattens below for examples and their notes explaining design decisions.
_guide.moving_a_building_or_tower: Edit buildings[] or towers[]. pos is [X, Y, Z] where Y is CLEARANCE ABOVE GROUND (not absolute world height). yaw is rotation in degrees (0=+X, 90=+Z). Copy an existing entry and modify. Building pos.y is how high its floor rises above the land; tower/NPC pos.y is usually 0 (standing on the ground).
_guide.adding_a_flatten_pad: Each flat-bottomed structure (building, tower, staircase) NEEDS a flatten feature under it, 1 unit larger than the footprint so blending stays clear of walls. Add to heightfield.features with type='flatten', pos at structure's centre, size slightly larger than the structure, and falloff 10-12 (adjust higher for steeper terrain). If level is omitted, Heightfield computes it from the terrain itself.
_guide.adding_trees: Two kinds of tree source, don't confuse them. AMBIENT COVERAGE (everywhere, no edge, no gaps) is tree_scatter: a streamed grid, like grass and terrain — see tree_scatter_manager.gd. Its density comes from noise, not a placed list, so 'more trees everywhere' means raising trees_per_chunk_max or lowering bare_threshold there, not adding entries anywhere. LANDMARK STANDS (a specific named forest in a specific spot) are generators.mountain_trees and generators.forest: finite, hand-tuned, and deliberately NOT how you'd cover open ground (a finite list always has an edge — that's the whole reason tree_scatter exists). Add a new landmark stand by copying one of those two blocks; add ambient coverage everywhere by tuning tree_scatter, never by adding more generators.
_guide.adding_an_npc: Edit npcs[] array. Required: scene (must be 'witch' or 'medieval' as defined in zone_layout.gd), pos. Optional: wander_radius (how far the NPC roams; omit if you want them to stand still). Copy an existing entry and modify.
_guide.adding_a_prop: Edit props[] array. Required: scene ('rock', 'wall', 'pine_tree'), pos. Optional: yaw (rotation), scale (size multiplier, default 1.0), sink (how deep to bury it in the ground). Copy an existing entry and modify.
_guide.tweaking_atmosphere_grass_terrain: Edit terrain_manager, atmosphere, grass_manager dicts. These control rendering, fog, grass density, etc. All are optional — each class has its own defaults. See zone_layout.gd's SECTION_FIELD_TYPES for the full list of valid keys.

spawn.note: pos[1] (Y) is clearance ABOVE the ground, not a world height — every pos in this file follows the same convention, since the land undulates. See zone.gd's header.

features.note: Was the 'SouthHill' TerrainMound. Same centre, radius and height, so the same hill stands in the same place — it is simply described now rather than built.

EastMountain — a scale test for rolling/features and a proving ground for a large landmark. 200m across, nearest foot 20m east of spawn (spawn.x=10, foot at x=30, centre = foot + 100m radius). height=47 with noise=1.5 measures a peak slope of ~38 degrees (see feature_max_slope_degrees), matching SouthHill's proven-climbable steepness, safely under the player's 50 degree limit even before mesh smoothing. Rounded summit by construction (smoothstep is flat-tangent at d=0), so the flatten pad below settles onto the true peak height with nothing to override.
StoneKeep, footprint 16x12 centred (-26,-14): one unit of margin all round so the blend never starts under a wall.

Terrace (20x20 centred (-25,20)) AND TerraceStairs (start z=32, climb to z=30): one pad spanning z 8..34 so both sit on the same level, plus a unit of margin on x. The terrace pad deliberately covers its staircase — stairs rise a fixed amount to meet the plate above, so the ground at both ends must be the SAME level, or the top step falls short of the terrace or runs through it.

EastMountain summit: a level 20x20 platform for EastMountainTower — comfortably larger than the tower's own derived 8.4x8.4 footprint. The feature above is a PLATEAU, not a hill: its flat_ratio already holds the top exactly level out to radius 15, past this pad's own half-extent (10, ~14.1 at the rounded corners), so this pad has almost nothing to reconcile and only erases the noise ripple. A plain 'hill' was tried first: pinning a flat core near its curved summit forced the pad's shoulder to make up, in one falloff band, height the raw hill spreads over a much longer radius — 53.9 degrees at a 10-unit falloff, worse (52.9) at 36, because widening the band just reached further into the hill's own steepest ground. The plateau's genuinely flat top avoids the whole fight.

SouthValley. An ellipse rather than a rectangle on purpose so nothing about it reads as a built structure — every edge is curved. size (40x80) is the genuinely level core requested; the 60-unit falloff band is not a look, it is what the player's 50 degree floor_max_angle FORCES for a 30m-deep pad — a smoothstep's steepest point is 1.5x its average slope, so 30m of drop needs at least 1.5*30/tan(50deg) = ~57 units of run even with zero noise on top; 60 leaves a couple of degrees of margin once noise is added. That is also why the overall footprint (half + falloff, ~160x200) dwarfs the 40x80 core: a valley this deep cannot be climbed out of any faster than that. noise is deliberately large next to every other feature's (1.5-1.9) — 'very bumpy' was the explicit ask, verified against find_unclimbable_features rather than guessed. Centred (10, 220): due south of spawn (10, 22, 'south' = +Z per camera_rig.gd's compass convention), far enough to clear the mountains_protected radius (reaches to z=102 here), the forest band (anchor at z~90), and EastMountain (centred x=130, 120 units away in x alone, past its own 100-unit radius regardless of z).

terrain_manager.note: Tiles GROW with distance: chunk_size is the innermost tile, doubling each of ring_count rings outward (32/64/128/256/512). max_screen_error_px picks the ring from projected screen size, not a fixed-distance ladder. Only ring 0 gets collision. horizon_distance is the hard edge past which nothing builds — pushing it out wants distance fog first or the edge is plainly visible. skirt_depth is the level-0 apron; verify_zone_layout.gd measures the real gaps against this land.

atmosphere.note: The two fog distances are FRACTIONS of terrain_manager.horizon_distance, not metres, so pushing the horizon out moves the haze with it. shadow_distance is NOT derived — it's a fixed texel budget; stretching it to the horizon would just blur near shadows to buy shadows the fog already hides.

grass_manager.note: load_radius is sized to clear everything the isometric camera can show a bit past default zoom in any rotation, so a chunk should never visibly pop in or out.

grass_exclusions.note: Terrace: centred (-25, 20), 20 x 20. Grass under a solid plate is invisible and still costs a blade.
EastMountainTower: footprint is derived from its stair geometry rather than authored (see tower.gd), so it is asked directly rather than duplicated here as a literal.

plates.name: Terrace
plates.note: A raised terrace on the far side of the map, to prove the system handles more than one elevation.

staircases.name: TerraceStairs
staircases.note: Rise 1.5 (5 x step_height 0.3), must exactly match the Terrace plate's height — see the Terrace flatten pad's note above.

buildings.name: StoneKeep
buildings.note: Turned to put the front door on the north face — the default camera looks toward -X/-Z, so a door on the -Z face would never be seen.

towers.name: EastMountainTower
towers.note: Sits on the EastMountain summit flatten pad, inside mountain_trees' clear_radius. yaw 90 puts the door on the WEST face — verified with a headless probe of Basis(UP, yaw) against compass.gd's convention — approached from the mountain's western shoulder, where the treeline and the climbable slope both are. No 'size': the tower solves its own footprint from its stair geometry.

props.note: Rocks sit half-buried anyway; sink hides the sliver of ground a sphere leaves visible on a slope.
Six metres long, so on rolling ground one end lifts clear without a deeper sink — 0.5 covers the worst this land does across that span; a wall on genuinely steep ground would need a real foundation.

These five pines are STALE, as warned in the original code: originally strung along Wind.direction_degrees (-45) so a gust reached one after the next. direction_degrees is now 90 and these hand-placed positions were never re-laid to match — they still catch gusts correctly (gust_total() samples wherever a tree actually stands), they just no longer form a deliberate line along the wind. The forest generator below reads Wind.direction_degrees live and has no such staleness risk; prefer that pattern over hardcoded positions for anything meant to stay aligned with the wind axis.

mountain_trees.note: EastMountain's tree cover: tight clumps plus a sparse fill between them, so the slope reads as a real treeline. Confined to an annulus — inside clear_radius stays bare for the tower, outside outer_radius stays clear of the steepest rim ground. clump_radius_margin (8.0) keeps clumps from anchoring right at the rim (clumps roll their radius up to outer_radius - clump_radius_margin). Deterministic: seed only, per DESIGN_GOALS.md's 'keep generated content seeded' rule.

forest.note: A dense pine forest well clear of spawn, laid out as a band ROTATED 90 DEGREES FROM the small hand-placed cluster in props: rows run along Wind's live direction axis (so a gust sweeps down a row, tree after tree) and the band itself is long in the perpendicular axis, so the forest reads as a mass from any angle. anchor (-40, 90) sits well past the small pine cluster and the SouthHill feature (centred (-46,-46), radius ~24) so the two stands don't overlap and neither clips the hill's steeper ground. align_to_wind=true means the generator reads Wind.direction_degrees live at build time (falling back to 90.0, wind.gd's own declared default, in the editor where the Wind autoload isn't fully set up) — see zone.gd's _generate_forest for why hardcoding the angle a second time caused the props-list pines above to drift stale.

tree_scatter.note: Ambient tree cover, everywhere, forever — the fix for 'trees run out if I walk far enough'. mountain_trees and forest above are AUTHORED landmarks (a specific treeline, a specific windbreak); this is background scatter with no edge, built the same way grass and terrain already are: as a streamed grid of chunks around the player rather than a finite pre-placed list. Every chunk's tree count comes from LOW-FREQUENCY NOISE sampled at its centre (noise_frequency 0.012 -> features roughly 80m across, i.e. copse- and glade-sized, not continent-sized), keyed by chunk coordinate and this seed, so the same chunk always regrows the same trees — no save data needed, same principle as heightfield's noise layers. trees_per_chunk_floor guarantees at least one candidate tree per chunk regardless of the noise roll, which is the actual fix for 'large bare areas': nowhere is a hard zero by construction, only sparser or denser. bare_threshold is where noise stops adding anything ABOVE the floor, so patches below it read as sparse rather than forested; well below 0 on purpose so genuinely empty ground stays rare, not half the map. clear_radius keeps a ring around spawn empty (uses spawn_pos from this same file as its centre) so the starting view isn't cluttered. See tree_scatter_manager.gd for the streaming mechanics and scripts/world/zone.gd's get_tree_scatter/_make_tree_scatter_manager for wiring.
